proofs: Existing local sequence is not advanced or reset by adoption, authoritative allocation or delivery.
Confirmed and quarantined IDs, outbox payloads/hashes, records, receipts, corporate call contents and legacy schema hash are preserved.
New calls have no internal ID until a committed authoritative reservation; capture can complete durably without MADM.
Concurrent reservers receive disjoint int32 IDs; direct writers register their IDs or are rejected by the same registry key.
A competing writer waits for an uncommitted reservation and then cannot consume its ID.
A separate SQL role cannot read tokens, disable the guard or use another roles token.
Adopting intent is durable before remote changes, and capture does not wait for the remote adoption commit.
Remote allocation/adoption commit followed by local failure or uncertain local commit recovers idempotently with the same IDs/tokens.
Concurrent materialization/delivery confirms each call once; resume respects adoption lock order.
At int32 exhaustion, calls remain durably unallocated; no wrap, arbitrary numeric range, MAX-based allocator or fallback nextval is used.
Legacy record writers without authoritative assignments are rejected by a deferred local database fence.
Migrations are idempotent; old quarantine and verification/recovery remain functional.
adoption_requirements: Reviewed local migration 008 and corporate migration corporate/001_id_allocator.sql; no migrations were run outside disposable test databases.
Same updated worker already running; pause only delivery, prepare durable adopting mode, install DBA-approved corporate guard, adopt using original request UUID.
Guard applies to every corporate writer; privileged DDL bypass or registry tampering is outside the exclusivity contract.
Runtime grants are USAGE/EXECUTE for the corporate reservation API; do not grant direct registry/counter access.
All existing local IDs are registered without remapping; previously known collisions still need the existing selective recovery procedure.
